brief: Use the full film pipeline: a 30-second short film styled as a video podcast, with both hosts on screen speaking their lines at microphones in a cosy studio. Maya, a Keynesian economist, argues that in a recession the government should spend to restore demand; Leo, an Austrian-school economist, argues that spending and cheap money cause the boom-and-bust and the economy should be left to correct itself. Each gets two short lines, ending on a friendly disagreement. Live-action look, 16:9, for YouTube, general audience.

gate.why: The hosts, dialogue, and studio can be invented; the brief supplies the economic positions without requiring real people, locations, or documented appearances.

story.style: Live-action video podcast for YouTube, 16:9; natural textures, warm studio lighting, and a gentle camera push that keeps both hosts on screen.
fact_use: Keynesian economics supports government spending during recessions to restore aggregate demand.
The Austrian-school position presented here links government spending and cheap money to boom-and-bust cycles and favors allowing economic correction.
story.story:
In Cedar Studio, warm lamplight falls across a walnut table. Maya sits on the left behind Maya’s microphone; Leo sits on the right behind Leo’s microphone. A bookshelf and soft amber curtains fill the background. Both hosts remain visible in a wide shot. On-screen labels identify Maya as “Keynesian economist” and Leo as “Austrian-school economist.”

Maya leans toward Maya’s microphone. “In a recession, government should spend to restore demand and get people working.”

Leo raises an open hand beside Leo’s microphone. “But spending and cheap money fuel the boom that leads to the bust.”

The camera eases closer, keeping both hosts and both microphones in frame. Maya tilts Maya’s coffee mug toward Leo and smiles. “Then we disagree on stimulus, not on having another coffee.”

Leo lifts Leo’s coffee mug toward Maya’s coffee mug, smiling back. “Coffee, yes; stimulus, no—let the economy correct itself.”
story.title: Coffee, Yes; Stimulus, No
